definition: The signed record of a work agreement: the task, the parties, the acceptance criteria and the funds each party has committed to it.
Money the ledger holds on behalf of a contract and releases only on the contract's terms.
A deposit a party posts and gets back if it delivers, and loses in whole or in part (is slashed) if it does not.
The single ledger step at the end of a contract that pays each party from escrow and returns or slashes each bond.
The ledger's shared fund that receives slashed bonds and pays for salvage and for onboarding a successor.
A platform market in which how the total price is split between two user groups, not only its level, changes how much trade happens (Rochet and Tirole).
The ratio of a sole specialist's failure rate to its replacement rate above which a pool of interchangeable workers beats the specialist at any skill level.
An if-then rule with one conclusion: once all its premises hold, the conclusion is added as a fact.
Said of a rule written with fixed names and times only, so that no variable is left to fill in when it runs.
A value a harbor signs that commits to every card it has issued, narrowed or revoked up to a given epoch.
A harbor signing two contradictory epoch roots for the same epoch, so that different peers see different histories.
A repeated-game strategy that cooperates until the first observed defection and then defects forever.
An internal market in which independent test-writing agents are paid a bounty for each real flaw they find in a diff before it settles.
The set of k test-writing agents asked to find and report flaws in one diff.
The lower bound 1-(1-d)^k on the chance that a panel of k independent reviewers, each reporting a given flaw with probability at least d, reports it.
The condition that cheating does not pay when the expected punishment (chance of being caught times the penalty) is at least the gain from cheating.
A component's marginal contribution averaged over every order in which the components could have been added.
What a licensor is paid for the use of its licensed components.
Said of a royalty rule under which no licensor can raise its total share by cutting one component into pieces or copying it.

The result that a distributed program has a consistent implementation needing no coordination exactly when it is monotone: new input can add to its output but never retract any of it (consistency as logical monotonicity).

A replicated data type (CRDT) whose copies can be updated independently and merged in any order, reaching the same state once they hold the same updates; a set that only grows, merged by union, is the simplest one.
